result.summary: The intersection provides basic crossing markings but lacks critical accessibility features like curb ramps and pedestrian-specific signals. The environment is further constrained by narrow, obstructed sidewalks and poor sightlines due to the building's proximity to the roadway.

hazards.name: Lack of curb ramps
hazards.description: The absence of sloped transitions at the corner creates a significant barrier for users with mobility aids or strollers.
hazards.location_in_image: At the corner of the sidewalk near the crosswalk

hazards.name: Missing pedestrian signals
hazards.description: Pedestrians must rely on vehicle signals, which do not provide dedicated crossing phases or countdowns.

hazards.name: Sidewalk obstructions
hazards.description: Utility poles and traffic signal bases significantly narrow the effective width of the sidewalk.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the sidewalk edge near the building

hazards.name: Damaged pavement and debris
hazards.description: Cracked pavement and debris near the sewer grate create a trip hazard.

interventions.title: Install ADA-compliant curb ramps
interventions.description: Add tactile warning surfaces and sloped ramps at all crossing points to ensure accessibility.

interventions.title: Add pedestrian countdown signals
interventions.description: Install dedicated pedestrian signal heads with countdown timers to improve crossing safety.

interventions.title: Curb extensions (bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane to shorten crossing distance and improve visibility.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment features marked zebra crosswalks and sidewalks on both sides of the street, with traffic flow regulated by signals. However, the lack of dedicated pedestrian signals and the relatively wide, open roadway design increase exposure and potential for higher vehicle speeds.

hazards.name: Lack of pedestrian signals
hazards.description: No dedicated walk/don't walk signals are visible at the intersection, forcing pedestrians to rely on vehicle traffic lights.

hazards.name: Wide crossing distance
hazards.description: The width of the roadway increases the time pedestrians are exposed to traffic without any refuge or curb extensions.
hazards.location_in_image: Across the main roadway at the zebra crossing.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Countdown Signals
interventions.description: Install dedicated pedestrian signal heads with countdown timers to provide clear information on remaining crossing time.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Construct bulb-outs at the corners to shorten the crossing distance and improve sight lines between drivers and pedestrians.

result.summary: The intersection provides basic pedestrian infrastructure including sidewalks, curb ramps, and a marked crosswalk. However, safety is compromised by faded pavement markings, the absence of dedicated pedestrian signals, and a large vehicle obstructing sightlines at the crossing point.

hazards.name: Sightline Obstruction
hazards.description: A large delivery truck is parked near the intersection, significantly blocking the view between pedestrians and oncoming traffic.
hazards.location_in_image: Center, parked on the roadway adjacent to the crosswalk

hazards.name: Faded Crosswalk Markings
hazards.description: The zebra-style crosswalk markings are heavily worn, reducing their visibility to approaching motorists.

interventions.title: Intersection Daylighting
interventions.description: Restrict parking near the intersection to ensure clear sightlines between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk
interventions.description: Repaint the crosswalk with high-visibility continental markings to improve driver awareness.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Countdown Signals
interventions.description: Install dedicated pedestrian signal heads with countdown timers to provide clear crossing information.

result.summary: The street environment consists of a wide, unmarked asphalt roadway flanked by narrow concrete sidewalks in fair condition. There is a lack of formal pedestrian infrastructure at the foreground intersection, including missing crosswalk markings and curb ramps.

hazards.name: Unmarked crossing
hazards.description: The lack of visible crosswalk markings at the intersection increases the risk of vehicle-pedestrian conflicts.

hazards.name: Missing curb ramps
hazards.description: The absence of curb ramps at the corners limits accessibility for pedestrians with mobility impairments.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Paint continental-style crosswalks to clearly define pedestrian right-of-way and increase visibility.

interventions.title: ADA Curb Ramps
interventions.description: Install standard curb ramps with tactile warning pads at all intersection corners to ensure accessibility.

interventions.title: Street Trees
interventions.description: Plant street trees to provide a physical and psychological buffer between the sidewalk and the roadway.
